acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Gargoyles family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Cathedral Warden, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Tracery-Aisle Champion (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Marble and verdigris bronze construction, spired horns, ornate carved armor, and wings framed like window tracery.
Signature mechanic: Rose-Window Guard: one ornate wing frames a closing aisle while the opposite tracery panel vents through a water-spout mouth.
battlefieldDuty: Control alternating aisles by opening marble-and-bronze wing tracery as a load-bearing screen.
constructionDimensions: Material/structure branches: T1 chipped sandstone, tiny useless wings, perch chip, and crude water-spout mouth gain one crystal mortar key; T2 granite, moss, and small wings gain sediment-set hop joints; T3 broad wings, carved relief, and amber seams gain load ribs; T4 marble, bronze, and tracery gain fracture braces; T5 buttress wings, throne, and attendants gain bounded throne faults.

Motion/process branches: T1 one short perch drop loads the water-spout mortar key; T2 a hop with small wings commits one granite joint; T3 the dive with broad wings transfers load through relief ribs; T4 a tracery aisle plants through its bronze brace; T5 each attendant command loads and releases one throne fault.
counterplay: Take the open aisle and break the darkening bronze brace before the framed wing closes. Affinity signal: Affinity counterplay branches: T1 the chipped-sandstone perch and tiny wings expose the water-spout mortar fault after landing; T2 the granite moss line and small-wing hinge expose a loaded joint after the hop; T3 broad wings and amber relief seams expose a load-rib fracture after the dive; T4 marble, bronze, and tracery expose the committed brace; T5 buttress wings, throne, and attendants expose the commanded throne fault after its load releases.
identityInvariants: Squat crouched construction, hunched shoulders, horned beast face, clawed grip, and folded architectural wings remain recognizable.
Sandstone, granite, marble, bronze, mortar, moss, and water staining remain discrete built materials rather than flesh.
Relief carving, water-spout mouths, restrained amber seams, and pedestal fragments preserve the architectural source grammar.
Stone quality and wing architecture escalate from useless carved flaps to sovereign buttresses while load-bearing joints stay readable.
telegraph: Spired horns align with an aisle and verdigris bronze drains from the brace about to carry the marble wing.
